structured_output.summary: The gate failure was a flaky integration test, and the cause was a real gap in the byte accounting. A client's first bytes can already sit in the hijacked connection's read buffer. The proxy forwarded those to the backend but didn't add them to `bytes_to_backend`, so `TestStreamDetachedWithAccessLogging` sometimes saw 24 bytes instead of 25. I now count those buffered bytes in `streaming.go`. After the fix, the integration and reverseproxy packages passed on the final run and on several earlier reruns. I removed the temporary stderr redirect I had added to `TestMain` to read the failure. I did not rerun the caddyhttp, encode and intercept packages after this fix, and nothing else in them changed.

criteria_notes.note: TestStreamThroughEncode, TestStreamWebSocketThroughEncode, TestInterceptUpgradeThroughReverseProxy, TestReverseProxyHandleResponseUpgrade, the access-log tests, and the unit intercept/encode tests.
TestResponseRecorder* tests, TestHijackedConnUnwrap, TestEncode* hijack tests, TestUpgradedStreamBypassesRecorder.
TestStreamExtendedConnectOverH2 (default and detached); HTTP/1.1 detached upgrades are covered by the detached reload tests.
TestStreamAccountingCountsOnce, TestStreamAccountingFirstResultWins, TestUpgradedStreamAccounts* tests, TestInitReverseProxyMetricsRegistersStreamMetrics; buffered bytes are now counted too.
caddyfile_test.go, the reverse_proxy_stream_detached adapt test, TestStreamLoadRejectsInvalidLogLevel.
